figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Characterization of the type I-E CRISPR-Cas system in Streptomyces mobaraensis IPIO2. a. Genomic organization of type I-E CRISPR-Cas locus, including 
the cas gene cluster ( cas3-cas8-cas11-cas7-cas5-cas6-cas1-cas2 ) and the CRISPR array consisting of 19 repeats (black diamonds) and 18 spacers (rectangular colored 
squares). b. Predicted stem-loop structure of the crRNA in the endogenous type I-E CRISPR-Cas system. c. The putative protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) derived 
from bioinformatics analysis of protospacer 5 ′ -ﬂanking sequences using WebLogo. d, e. Plasmid interference assays validating the functional PAM. The number of 
exconjugants per 108 spores for each interference plasmid were averaged from two biological replicates. Gray represents the negative control; red indicates the 
functional PAM (5 ′ -AAC-3 ′ ) recognized by this the type I-E CRISPR-Cas system.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Repurposing the native type I-E CRISPR-Cas system for gene deletion in Streptomyces mobaraensis IPIO2. a. Schematic diagram of the editing plasmid pCRISPR- 
tg for tg gene deletion. b. Schematic diagram of the homologous recombination plasmid 1278-tg for tg gene deletion. c. (i) Two spacers within the tg gene were 
selected for CRISPR plasmid construction, along with two pairs of primers used to verify the tg deletion mutants. (ii, iii) PCR veriﬁcation of tg deletion eﬃciency in 
transformants obtained from thiostrepton selection (Round 1) using the primers TG-out-F/R (ii) and TG-in-F/R (iii). Two transformants carrying the control plasmid 
1278-tg served as negative controls. M: 1 kb plus DNA marker; P: pCRISPR-tg-1/2 plasmid as template; G: IPIO2 genome as template. Lanes 1-–10: individual 
transformants. d. Transglutaminase (TGase) activity assay of the fermentation cultures of all transformants. Transformants with successful tg deletion lost the ability 
to produce TGase, while the mixed-genotype transformants exhibited a marked decrease in TGase activity. e. PCR analysis of single colonies derived from pCRISPR- 
tg-1–1 transformants after plasmid curing (Round 2) using primers TG-out-F/R. M: 1 kb plus DNA marker; P: pCRISPR-tg-1 plasmid as template; G: IPIO2 genome (as 
template). Lanes 1–− 19: individual colonies. f. PCR analysis of single colonies derived from 1278-tg-1 transformants after plasmid curing (Round 2) using primers 
TG-out-F/R. M: 1 kb plus DNA marker; P: 1278-tg plasmid as template; G: IPIO2 genome (as template). Lanes 1–− 19: individual colonies.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Deletion of the downregulated genes identiﬁed through comparative proteomics. a. Volcano plot of the comparative proteomics data. Each dot represents a 
quantiﬁed protein. Blue dots indicate the expression ratio of at 24 h versus that at 16 h, and red dots indicate the expression ratio of at 42 h versus that at 24 h. The 
horizontal dashed line represents the signiﬁcance threshold (p ≤ 0.05; —log10 p-value ≥ 1.3), and the vertical dashed lines denote the 2-fold increase (right, log2 
fold change ≥ 1) or decrease (left, log2 fold change ≤ –− 1) thresholds. Six proteins ( ≥ 2-fold decrease in both 24 h/16 h and 42 h/24 comparisons, p ≤ 0.05) are 
labeled with their protein IDs. b. Transglutaminase (TGase) activity of four mutants (IPIO2 Δ42, IPIO2 Δ1044/1045, IPIO2 Δ1204, and IPIO2 Δ957) and the wild-type 
IPIO2. Error bars represent the mean ± SD standard deviation (n = 3 biological replicates). ∗ p < 0.05; ∗ ∗ p < 0.01; ∗ ∗ ∗ p < 0.001; ns, not signiﬁcant (two-tailed paired 
t -tests). c. SDS-PAGE analysis of the fermentation cultures of four mutants and the wild-type IPIO2. Denser TGase bands in the mutant strains indicate enhanced 
TGase production. d. Biomass of four mutants and the wild-type IPIO2. n = 3 biological replicates.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. The endogenous CRISPR-Cas- system mediated mediates genome editing for large DNA deletions. a. Schematic illustration of the pum biosynthesis gene 
cluster (BGC) (11.8 kb) deletion in IPIO2. b. PCR screening of four pum BGC-deleted transformants obtained through thiostrepton selection using two pairs of primers 
indicated in Fig. Fig. 4 a. The predicted size of the PCR products was 828 bp (yellow squarerectangle) using for pum-out-F/R, while no band was observed for using 
pum-in-F/R, in the deletion strains. M: 1 kb plus DNA marker; P: pCRISPR-pum (as a control); G: Genomic DNA of IPIO2 (as a control). Lanes 1–− 4: diﬀerent 
numbers of the transformants. c. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis of pseudouridimycin ( m/z 487.1896 [M + H] + ) from the fermentation 
extracts of the IPIO2 Δpum transformants. d. Schematic illustration of the pie BGC (40.1 kb) deletion in IPIO2 Δpum. e. PCR veriﬁcation of ﬁve pie BGC-deleted 
transformants obtained through thiostrepton selection using two pairs of primers indicated in Fig. Fig. 4 d The predicted size of PCR products was 696 bp (yellow 
square rectangle) using for pie-out-F/R, while no band was observed using for pie-in-F/R, in the deletion strains. M: 1 kb plus DNA marker; P: pCRISPR-pie (as 
a control); G: Genomic DNA of IPIO2 Δpum (as a control). Lanes 1–− 5: diﬀerent numbers of the transformants. f. LC-MS analysis of piericidin A1 ( m/z 416.2795 
[M + H] + ) from the fermentation extracts of the IPIO2 Δpum Δpie transformants. g. TGase activity of the edited strain IPIO2 Δpum Δpie. h. Biomass of IPIO2 Δpum Δpie. 
Error bars represent the mean ± SD standard deviation (n = 3 biological replicates). ∗ p < 0.05; ∗ ∗ p < 0.01; ∗ ∗ ∗ p < 0.001; ns, not signiﬁcant (two-tailed paired 
t -tests).
